headline: GOLD BOUNCES FROM 15-MONTH LOW — Spot Recovers to $3,565 on Thin Thanksgiving Session; Bulls Need $3,697 to Signal Reversal
snippet: Spot gold recovered to $3,565 per ounce on Thursday November 26 after Wednesday's plunge to $3,446 on hotter-than-expected core PCE data had taken the metal to its lowest level since August 2025. With US markets closed for Thanksgiving, volume is thin and price discovery limited; technicians have set $3,697 as the first resistance that would signal genuine reversal and $3,446 as the floor bulls must now defend heading into Monday's reopening.

headline: COPPER SURGES 2.65% FROM 2026 LOW — Tariff-Fear Easing Triggers Recovery Toward $12,000 as Physical Premiums Hold Firm
snippet: LME three-month copper rose 2.65% to near $11,958 per tonne on November 26, snapping a two-day rout that had taken prices to their 2026 low below $12,000 for the first time since March as a moderate easing of US tariff headlines let the market reprice the still-tight physical market. The partial rebound confirms that physical demand — with Yangshan import premiums still near $450/t — is not collapsing at these prices, even as the broader 20% decline from September's record high remains intact.

headline: LEEUWIN METALS SNAPS UP WA GOLD IN ALL-SCRIP DEAL — 49.3% Premium Locks In 897,000oz on Granted Mining Leases
snippet: Leeuwin Metals (ASX: LM1) agreed to acquire WA Gold (ASX: WAU) in a binding all-scrip scheme of arrangement, paying 1 Leeuwin share per 11.72 WA Gold shares — a 49.3% premium to WA Gold's last close — with the combined entity holding 896,600 ounces of gold on granted Mining Leases in Western Australia. All-scrip consolidation at a near-50% premium in a down market signals that the acquirer is treating current prices as a floor and using its own equity as currency before a gold price recovery reprices the target.

headline: 10,000-METRE DRILL PROGRAM LAUNCHES IN QUÉBEC'S ABITIBI GOLD BELT — Opawica Explorations Targets High-Grade Gold at Rouyn-Noranda
snippet: Opawica Explorations announced on November 25 the launch of a 10,000-metre drill program at its gold project in the Rouyn-Noranda region of Québec's Abitibi gold belt — one of the world's highest-grade gold-producing regions, neighbouring the Horne and LaRonde camps measured in tens of millions of ounces. Drilling into the Abitibi at the bottom of the gold price cycle is the counter-cyclical move that historically produces the best-returning exploration programs, as results arrive in hand before any price recovery begins.

headline: IMAGINE LITHIUM MOBILIZES DRILLS AT JACKPOT — Casino Royale and Ruth Pegmatite Targets Activated for Fall 2026 Program
snippet: Imagine Lithium (TSXV: ILI) announced the commencement of its Fall 2026 drill program at the Jackpot lithium project, with rigs now mobilized to test the Casino Royale extension and the Ruth Pegmatite target. With Citi having cut its three-year lithium price forecast by 40% and spodumene markets expected to remain in surplus through 2028, explorers that keep drilling through the bear market are building the resource inventory that will command a premium when the cycle turns.

headline: URANIUM AT $90/LB BUT MINERS DOWN 50% FROM HIGHS — The Sector Paradox Retail Investors Need to Understand Before 2027
snippet: An analysis of November 2026 uranium sector dynamics identifies a stark divergence: spot uranium holds in the high $80s per pound and the long-term contract price rose 10% to $97/lb, yet the Sprott Uranium Miners ETF (URNM) is down roughly 56% from its January 2026 high of $84.95, with Uranium Energy Corp (UEC), Energy Fuels (UUUU) and peers at or near 52-week lows. The analysis evaluates the five main uranium equity vehicles — CCJ, UEC, UUUU, SRUUF and NXE — and what each faces as the market heads into 2027.

headline: BARRICK, AGNICO AND KINROSS FACE ESTIMATE CUTS — Which Gold and Silver Miners Have a Cushion at 15-Month Lows
snippet: An Investing.com analysis identifies the gold and silver miners most vulnerable to earnings cuts at current 15-month price lows — with Barrick Mining, Agnico Eagle, and Kinross Gold flagged for downward estimate revisions — while separating them from producers with lower all-in sustaining costs and unhedged balance sheets that provide a genuine price buffer. For retail investors deciding whether to hold, trim, or accumulate mining equity positions through the correction, knowing which names have cost-structure cushion versus which are earnings-sensitive at spot is the most actionable due-diligence filter available right now.

headline: INFINITY METALS ACQUIRES 80% OF NANADIE NORTH COPPER IN WA — $25K Cash + 35M Shares Stakes Ground in Murchison Copper Corridor
snippet: Infinity Metals (ASX: INF) agreed on November 26 to acquire an 80% interest in the Nanadie North copper licence application in Western Australia for $25,000 cash and 35 million shares; the licence application has not yet been granted, so the deal remains subject to tenure approval. In WA's Murchison region, the Nanadie corridor has attracted renewed attention as copper-focused juniors secure ground positions ahead of any recovery in LME copper prices from their current 2026 lows.

headline: COLIBRI SIGNS LOI FOR SONORA COPPER-MOLY PROJECTS — All-Shares Deal Adds Los Verdes and Potreritos to Mexico Portfolio
snippet: Colibri signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire the Mexican subsidiary behind the Los Verdes and Potreritos copper-molybdenum projects in Sonora state, issuing 20 million common shares to Mining Americas — roughly 35.2% of Colibri's outstanding shares post-issuance — with no cash consideration. Copper-molybdenum porphyries in Sonora sit within one of North America's most prospective copper corridors; acquiring ground at all-shares terms during a down copper market is the classic pre-cycle land assembly move ahead of a potential LME recovery.

headline: GDXJ MOST OVERSOLD IN 4 YEARS as Junior Miners Report Earnings Beat — Contrarian Case for Gold Equities Builds Into Year-End
snippet: A November 2026 Investing.com analysis finds the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) trading at approximately 77.5% of its 200-day moving average — the most oversold level in four years — even as gold miners across the sector continued reporting earnings above consensus estimates despite rising operating costs. The divergence between strong fundamentals and historically depressed valuations is the foundational argument for the contrarian accumulation case in junior miners heading into 2027, particularly for investors with a 12-to-24-month time horizon.
